question: Which L2 regularization strength gives the lowest 5-fold cross-validated Brier score?
rationale: Grid search across specified lambda values using contiguous block cross-validation with full-batch gradient descent (200 iterations, lr=0.1) following exact fitting conventions. Brier score is the standard proper scoring rule for classification.
decision: Grid search all 5 lambda values with contiguous 5-fold CV, compute mean Brier scores, select lambda with minimum CV Brier
expected_effect: Identify optimal regularization strength that minimizes overfitting while maintaining model fit quality. Improvement over baseline (lambda=0) should be positive if regularization helps, zero/negative if not.
falsifier: If any lambda value produces invalid Brier scores (outside [0,1] for well-calibrated model), the fitting procedure has an error

question: Do interaction features significantly improve model performance?
alternatives: Fit raw features only with lambda=0.1
Fit raw features + interaction features (x0*x1, x1*x2, x2*x3, x0*x3) with lambda=0.1
rationale: Paired t-test across 5 folds comparing raw model Brier to interaction model Brier. Under null hypothesis of no difference, t-statistic follows t(4) distribution. t>2.0 provides approximately p<0.10 evidence for one-tailed test at df=4.
decision: Fit both models, compute per-fold Brier differences, run paired t-test, report t-stat and interaction_helps=(t>2.0)
expected_effect: If interactions are useful, raw Brier > interaction Brier (positive differences), yielding t>0. interaction_helps true only when t exceeds 2.0 threshold indicating substantial improvement.
falsifier: If paired t-test cannot be computed (e.g., insufficient variation across folds), the comparison is not valid

question: Which compression configuration (sparsity × quantization) best retains dense model performance?
rationale: Fit dense model once on all rows with lambda=0.1. For each config: apply sparsity (zero smallest |w|), apply quantization (map to 2^bits uniform levels), measure in-sample Brier. Retention = dense_brier / compressed_brier. Select config with highest retention.
decision: Grid search all 6 (sparsity, bits) pairs, compute retention for each, select pair with maximum retention
expected_effect: Highly sparse/low-bit configs may degrade performance (low retention), while moderate compression preserves performance (retention near 1.0). Best config balances compression and accuracy.
falsifier: If retention is undefined (compressed_brier=0 or NaN) for any config, that config is invalid and excluded
